questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet:

options.text: Allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see everything you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Has little impact on whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see and be seen by others. Good positioning also protects you from wind blasts created by nearby vehicles.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Clothing of any color because drivers can easily see you in daylight.
Dark-colored clothing to contrast with bright sunlight.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Always wear bright clothing to stay visible, even in the day.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use the rear brake before the front brake.

questions.explanation: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time for a quick stop.

questions.question: If you have only one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding skills. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to change to red.
The light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that the signal will change to red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: You can increase your chances of being seen at an intersection by:
questions.explanation: Use your headlight at all times. This improves your chances of being seen at intersections.

questions.question: As your motorcycle accelerates, you will need to:
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle accelerates, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locking your brakes makes you lose control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If you lock your rear brake on a surface with good grip while stopping, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles going under 25 mph. These include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be checked often by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked often by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular habit.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, focus most on the helmet's:
questions.explanation: Protection should be your main concern when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you stay balanced.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, signal your moves to others, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready for changes.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Allowed when stopped at traffic lights.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is very dangerous. It increases crash risk by up to 23 times. South Dakota law prohibits texting while operating a vehicle.

questions.question: Mirrors on motorcycles:

options.text: Have no blind spots because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the left third of the lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this position?

options.text: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can make side mirrors hard to use.
Drivers should never use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This way, the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes when you need to stop.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after that hour passes.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not make sudden moves on a slippery surface. Any quick change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Move smoothly when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
